title: Introduce stage-aware trace enricher and cost-hash anchors
author: Miguel Santos
body: Context: long-running invocations with multiple model stages (tokenize -> encode -> decode -> postprocess) were difficult to attribute for token-level cost and latency because spans often lacked a lightweight stage tag and a deterministic cost fingerprint. This PR introduces a stage-aware trace enricher that annotates spans with a stable token_cost_hash and stage tags at ingestion time, exposes a small KV hitmap for stage-level warmup and latency skew, and adds dashboard panels and alert tuning for stage-specific regressions. Motivation: make it cheaper and more precise to detect which model stage is driving tail latency or token cost regressions, and enable sampled enrichment on high-cardinality routes without blowing up trace volume. What I changed: 1) telemetry/enricher: new StageTraceEnricher component that inspects invocation metadata and model pipeline config and injects span tags: stage (tokenize|encode|kv_cache|decode|post), token_cost_hash (64-bit hex), stage_seq (integer). The hash is deterministic from {model_version, route_id, prompt_shape_bucket, stage_name} so it can be used as an anchor for rollups. 2) tracing/ingestion: lightweight in-line tag propagation and an opt-in sharded enrichment queue to avoid backpressure on the trace pipeline. 3) metrics: new histogram metrics token_cost_by_stage_ms and token_cost_by_stage_tokens with labels {tenant, route, stage, cost_hash}. The histograms are compacted at rollup time to cap cardinality. 4) dashboards: added "Stage Cost Ladder" and "Stage Skew Heatmap" panels to the Observability -> Invocation Cost dashboard; panels include example queries and links to sampled trace drilldowns. 5) alerts: introduced stage-specific SLO guardrails that apply a dynamic suppression window when a single stage's token_cost_hash accounts for >70% of cost delta across an hour. 6) SDK: added a small helper call in the Python SDK to opt invocation metadata into stage enrichment (redwood.sdk.observe.set_stage_enrichment). Testing & rollout: unit tests for the enricher, integration test that replays synthetic invocations through the enrichment queue, and a canary rollout plan that enables enrichment for 2% of traffic on a single non-prod tenant for 48 hours. Backwards compatibility: traces that don't opt-in are unchanged; the enricher is behind a feature flag (telemetry.stage_enrichment_enabled) by default off for existing customers. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration replay [x] dashboard panels added [x] alert rule PR for monitoring repo created [x] performance benchmark (ingestion latency < +1ms p50 per enriched invocation). Impact: adds low-cardinality stage tags and a deterministic cost-hash to make downstream aggregation robust while keeping trace cardinality bounded. Rollout notes: enable feature flag in staging, validate cost_hash stability across minor model version bumps, then progressively enable per-team with A/B monitoring.
commits: telemetry: add StageTraceEnricher and unit tests
tracing: propagate stage tags and token_cost_hash at ingestion
metrics: introduce token_cost_by_stage histograms and compact rollup
dashboard: add Stage Cost Ladder and Stage Skew Heatmap panels
ci: add integration replay job for stage enrichment
review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: Design looks solid. Two asks: ensure token_cost_hash length is documented and add a migration note for the dashboards if customers backfill historical data.

Miguel Santos (author): Addressed both requests; added documentation section on hash format (64-bit hex) and dashboard backfill notes. Confirmed backfill is optional and dashboards fall back when cost_hash absent.
Jonah Becker: Concern about ingestion latency under high QPS. Can we make the enrichment queue bounded and add an async drop metric?

Miguel Santos (author): Added sharded bounded queue and an enrichment.drops_total metric; added a fallback path that emits a lightweight span tag 'enrichment_skipped' so downstream tooling knows enrichment was not applied.
Priya Raman: Alerts look noisy during deployments due to short-lived stage hash churn. Recommend a short dampening window and requiring a sustained >15m signal before firing.
Miguel Santos (author): Tuned alert to require sustained 15m and added auto-suppress for deploy-tagged traces. Also added a guidance comment to the alert rule.
ci_checks: integration-replay: fail (flaky under initial run) -> rerun
release_notes: Adds an opt-in stage enrichment pipeline that annotates spans with stage and token_cost_hash, stage-level histograms and dashboard panels, and stage-aware alert tuning. Enrichment is behind a feature flag and rolled out as a canary. Backwards compatible when disabled.
